xhs.content:
Your top SKU might already be wearing a label that quietly drops conversion 20-40%. You won't get notified.

It's called Frequently Returned. Amazon attaches it when a product's return rate sits above the category baseline, and it shows up directly on the detail page where every shopper sees it.

The brutal part: Amazon doesn't tell you. If you're not actively pulling returns reports, you might be wearing the badge for weeks while you keep paying for the same ad clicks that now convert at half the rate.

What triggers it:
• Return rate above category average
• Returns clustering around "not as described" or "quality issues"
• Post-promo spikes — exactly what happens after Prime Day or spring sales

Once flagged, you need weeks of below-average returns to remove it. Prime Day won't wait.

Three things to do this week if you sell physical products on Amazon:

1. Pull the FBA returns report. For every SKU, log return rate and the top three return reasons.
2. For SKUs above category average, fix the detail page first — real photos, sizing chart, materials, expectations. Buyers refund what didn't match what they thought they were buying.
3. For SKUs that are persistently broken and can't be fixed in 4-5 weeks, pause ads or remove them before Prime Day amplifies the problem.

The operator move here isn't "work harder" — it's deciding which SKUs to stop spending behind, before the platform decides for you.

What's your audit cadence on returns?
